candidates.description:

River Basin, Four Corners/Upper Dolores River, Northwest San Juan

* IMPACTS...Flooding will be possible over burn scars, at low-water
crossings, and along creeks, streams, washes, arroyos and other
flood-prone locations. Creeks and streams may rise out of their
banks. Unpaved roads could become muddy and impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

Hurricane Polo, are expected to produce numerous showers and

Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

in an elevated threat of property damage to homes and

waterfront along tidal rivers and bays resulting in some road

travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through

candidates.headline: Flood Warning issued September 27 at 11:53AM EDT until September 29 at 11:00PM EDT by NWS Boston/Norton MA
candidates.description:
...The National Weather Service in Norton has issued a Flood Warning
for the following rivers in Massachusetts...

Taunton River Near Bridgewater affecting Plymouth and Bristol
Counties.

For the Taunton River...including Bridgewater...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Taunton River near Bridgewater.

* WHEN...From this evening to Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Backwater flooding from the Taunton River
will cause flooding of lower Purchade Brook in Middleboro.  This
will cause Woloski Park to become impassable by most vehicles for
an extended period of time.  Beware of the dangers of crossing
flooded roadways. The water may be deeper than you think.
Floodwaters have the ability to damage roadways. Heed the advice of
local officials, and evacuate if asked to do so.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:45 AM EDT Sunday the stage was 5.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
this evening to a crest of 9.4 feet early tomorrow afternoon. It
will then fall below flood stage Tuesday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 9.4
feet on 03/25/2024.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
candidates.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at midnight EDT.

candidates.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued September 27 at 6:02AM EDT until September 27 at 6:00PM EDT by NWS Upton NY
candidates.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, 2 to 2 1/2 feet of
inundation above ground level in vulnerable areas near the
waterfront and shoreline. For the High Surf Advisory, large
breaking waves of 6 to 8 feet in the surf zone. For the High
Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Southwest Suffolk and Southern Nassau Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 6 PM EDT this
evening. For the High Surf Advisory, until 8 PM EDT this
evening. For the High Rip Current Risk, through this evening.

* COASTAL FLOOD IMPACTS...Widespread moderate to locally major
flooding of vulnerable areas near the waterfront and
shoreline. Flooding could again extend inland into coastal
areas that typically don't experience coastal flooding.
Coastal flooding will be exacerbated along north facing
shorelines from wave action, particularly for the barrier
island from Atlantic Beach, Long Beach to Jones Beach. This
will result in numerous road closures and cause widespread
flooding of low lying property including parking lots, parks,
lawns, and homes and businesses with basements near the
waterfront. Vehicles parked in vulnerable areas near the
waterfront will likely become flooded.

* SHOREFRONT AND BEACH IMPACTS...Breaking waves of 6 to 8 feet
along with elevated water levels will result in widespread
dune erosion and beach flooding. Localized overwashes are
possible where dune structures are compromised, resulting in
some flooding of roadways and vulnerable structures behind
protective dunes. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions
and localized beach erosion. Life threatening rip currents are
likely for all people entering the surf zone.
candidates.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Anyone visiting the beaches should stay out of the surf.

candidates.headline: Flood Watch issued September 27 at 1:44AM MST until September 29 at 9:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
candidates.areaDesc: Aguila Valley; Northwest Valley; Cave Creek/New River; Deer Valley; New River Mesa; Rio Verde/Salt River; Fountain Hills/East Mesa; Superior; Apache Junction/Gold Canyon; Tonto Basin; Mazatzal Mountains; Pinal/Superstition Mountains; San Carlos; Dripping Springs; Globe/Miami; Southeast Gila County
candidates.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of south central Arizona, including the following
areas, Aguila Valley, Apache Junction/Gold Canyon, Cave Creek/New
River, Deer Valley, Dripping Springs, Fountain Hills/East Mesa,
Globe/Miami, Mazatzal Mountains, New River Mesa, Northwest Valley,
Pinal/Superstition Mountains, Rio Verde/Salt River, San Carlos,
Southeast Gila County, Superior and Tonto Basin.

* WHEN...From late Monday night through Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The combination of deep tropical moisture moving into the area
from the south and an approaching weather disturbance from the
west will result in showers and thunderstorms capable of
producing localized heavy rainfall. Moderate to heavy rainfall
rates in excess of 1-2 inches per hour are expected. Some areas
will see training of storms leading to heavier rainfall
accumulations.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
candidates.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

* WHERE...Areas along and west of the central mountain chain

candidates.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive and long duration rainfall.

* WHERE...All of northern and central Arizona.

* WHEN...From Sunday evening through Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding will be possible over burn areas, low-water
crossings, creeks, streams, washes and swimming holes. Larger
creeks and rivers may exceed bankfull. Flooding of paved roads and
highway underpasses will be possible. Unpaved roads could become
muddy and impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Low pressure will interact with tropical moisture from the
eastern Pacific. This could potentially produce numerous showers
and embedded thunderstorms, with heavy rain that will fall over
saturated soils and burn scars. This could lead to localized
flash flooding and rises on local rivers, such as the Little
Colorado River.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
candidates.instruction:

Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

candidates.headline: Heat Advisory issued September 27 at 10:11AM AST until September 27 at 4:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
candidates.areaDesc: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; Southeast; Eastern Interior; North Central; Central Interior; Ponce and Vicinity; Northwest; Western Interior; Mayaguez and Vicinity; Southwest; Culebra; Vieques; St.Thomas...St. John.. and Adjacent Islands; St Croix
candidates.description:
* WHAT...This level of heat affects most individuals sensitive to
heat, especially those without effective cooling and/or adequate
hydration.

* WHERE...Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM AST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...High temperatures or elevated heat indices can worsen
symptoms in people with chronic conditions. They can also increase
the risk of heat-related illness among individuals sensitive to
heat with inadequate cooling or hydration. These risks are highest
across coastal areas, lowlands, interior valleys, and urban zones.
candidates.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.
